title: Saudi point-of-sale spending, Q3 2023 vs Q3 2022

attempts.text: In Q3 2023, the Saudi Arabia point-of-sale card spending (SAMA) showed a notable increase of 8.5% compared to the same quarter in 2022. The average weekly POS value rose to SAR 11.77 billion, marking a 290 million increase from SAR 11.48 billion in Q3 2022. This growth is attributed to an increase of 17.8% in the average weekly value, which stands at SAR 1,917 million. The Beverage and Food category saw a significant increase of 12.8% in its average weekly value, totaling SAR 1,811 million. In contrast, the Clothing and Footwear category experienced a decrease of 5.5% in its average weekly value, totaling SAR 695 million.

issues.detail: 'SAR 167 million' described as down but the fact is up
Restaurants & Café described as down but its change is up

attempts.text: In Q3 2023, the average weekly POS value increased by 8.5% compared to the same quarter in 2022. This significant increase is attributed to the Other category, which saw an increase of SAR 290 million, representing a 17.8% increase. The Beverage and Food category also experienced a notable increase of SAR 205 million, marking a 12.8% rise. Meanwhile, the Restaurants & Café category showed a slight increase of SAR 167 million, or 10.8% compared to the previous quarter. The Clothing and Footwear category experienced a decrease of SAR 41 million, marking a 5.5% decline. Lastly, the Jewelry category saw a decrease of SAR 38 million, or a 15.9% drop.

final_text: Average weekly point-of-sale spending in Saudi Arabia was SAR 11.77 bn in Q3 2023, up 8.5% from SAR 10.85 bn in Q3 2022. Average weekly transactions were 176.5 million (up 22.3%), and the average ticket was SAR 66.7 (down 11.3%). The largest movements were: Other increased by SAR 290 mn; Beverage and Food increased by SAR 205 mn; Restaurants & Café increased by SAR 167 mn.
